source_excerpts.text:
Material continuity

The inventory ledger treats functional stocks separately:

Each head and stem.
Each receiver lip and datum.
Each guide bore.
Each disc spring and its coating.
Retainer and cam/gear contact surfaces.
Approximately 0.20 g contained lubricant.

No planned critical-part replacement, replating or relubrication is allowed in the original 500-cycle test. Replacing one of four discs would replace 25% of that spring stock; it cannot be diluted by the housing mass.

The geometric constraint is stricter than the mass constraint. A worst new receiver/stem pair has only about 7 µm of clearance-growth allowance before reaching its proposed receiver limit. Much less than 5% metal loss could therefore invalidate the joint.

Wear residues, local profiles, guide clearances and lubricant loss must be measured directly. A clean appearance or a returned actuator position is not evidence that the local working geometry has returned.

title: Track critical working parts instead of diluting wear in a housing
